path.title: Reindeer Herders Cross Continents
path.summary: Permanent land allows Siberian reindeer herding, sled design, and cold-climate clothing techniques to spread gradually into Alaska by foot and caravan. Northern communities on both sides develop a shared seasonal round, exchanging breeding animals and knowledge each year.

path.title: Herders Map Interior River Routes
path.summary: Reindeer sled teams extend seasonal travel inland, producing route maps of Alaskan rivers, passes, and shelter sites shared among northern communities. This exploration is possible because reliable herds, sled designs, and cold-climate clothing from the cross-Beringian exchange reduce the risks of long winter journeys.
path.causalLink: The established cross-continental seasonal round created dependable herds, staging pastures, and guide knowledge that could be extended from coastal Beringia into Alaska's interior.

branches.title: Sled Teams Reach Great Slave Lake
branches.summary: Guided by the mapped Yukon and Tanana corridors, reindeer caravans reach the Mackenzie basin and Great Slave Lake, recording portages and winter pastures along the way. The journey follows from the parent maps because staged shelter sites and dependable herds turn a previously uncertain interior crossing into a repeatable seasonal route.
branches.scene: At dawn, sled teams glide across the frozen lake while guides unroll bark maps beside steaming reindeer enclosures.
branches.causalLink: The Fairbanks river-route maps, shelter lists, and staging herds provide the navigational chain and resupply points needed to extend travel eastward into the Mackenzie basin.

branches.title: Yukon Routes Meet Salmon Rivers
branches.summary: Following mapped southern tributaries, herding families reach Cook Inlet and exchange reindeer transport and tailored cold-weather clothing for salmon-processing knowledge. Mapped river travel makes this coastal contact repeatable, creating blended drying racks, sled designs, and seasonal food stores.
branches.scene: Reindeer sleds arrive above Cook Inlet as salmon strips glow orange on tall wooden drying racks.
branches.causalLink: Parent maps of Yukon and Tanana tributaries identify passes and shelter sites that let sled caravans descend safely toward Alaska's southern coast.

branches.title: Interior Pastures Improve Sled Reindeer
branches.summary: Herders use mapped interior pastures and sheltered valleys to maintain selected breeding herds through successive winters, gradually producing stronger reindeer suited to longer sled journeys. The parent route network makes this possible by revealing where fodder, wind shelter, and reliable water remain accessible in severe cold.
branches.scene: A herder measures antlers beside a Whitehorse corral as the strongest young reindeer are fitted with bright woven sled harnesses.
branches.causalLink: The parent maps identify winter pastures and shelter sites, allowing controlled year-round breeding instead of relying only on coastal seasonal herds.
